notes: Algorithm measured on AE 2026 8 bpc: tiles anchored at the layer's top-left; each tile = the mean of its PREMULTIPLIED RGBA pixels rounded to nearest (bit-exact up to 1 level), or with Sharp Colors (AE 3) the tile's LAST pixel (bottom-right: x = tile end - 1, y = tile end - 1), NOT its centre as Adobe's docs say (exact on all 800 tiles of 40x20). Tile of pixel x = floor(x*n/W) (integer maths), i.e. tile i spans [ceil(i*W/n), ceil((i+1)*W/n)); the visible refs only have W/n integer, so this rule for non-divisible sizes is the natural per-pixel one (consistent with the last-pixel sample = floor(((i+1)*W-1)/n)) but unverified: if AE instead cuts at floor(i*W/n) a 1-px column/row shifts at every boundary (13x7 on 640x360: mean 1.4 %, 2.9 % px > 8 between the two rules). Block counts are rounded to integers (AE integer sliders) and clamped to >= 1; counts above the layer size give 1-px tiles (identity). 4 separable passes, RGBA8 premultiplied intermediates: 0 = horizontal chunk mean over [x, min(x+K, tile end)), 1 = horizontal tile mean from the chunks, 2/3 = same vertically; K = 1 (copy) while a tile is <= 128 px, else ceil(sqrt(tile length)) so a pass stays <= ~max(128, 2*sqrt(L)) texelFetches (1 tile on 30000 px: 174). Sharp Colors: passes 0/2 copy, 1/3 fetch the last column/row (bit-exact). The intermediate rounding gives +-1 level vs AE's single rounding. Not reproduced: AE 4 Compositing Options (effect opacity / effect masks). The grid is computed on the canvas size, so keep the Rive node's `pad` at 0 (Mosaic never spills outside the layer).

measured.model_checks: offline vs exact numpy model (premultiplied tile mean / last pixel, floor(x*n/W) tiles) for 1x1, 2x1, 3x2, 4x3, 5x1, 13x7, 640x360, 1000x500 (chunked K>1 paths included) and sharp 13x7, 7x3, 1x1, 4000x4000: mean <= 0.049, max 1; Rive vs offline on 1x1, 3x2, 13x7, sharp 7x3, 2.6x1.2: mean <= 0.012, max 1
